hints: Notice the two curves at the same $x$: the large $10\text{ mm}$ amplitude curve is one progressive wave and the small $5\text{ mm}$ amplitude curve is the stationary wave.
Recall that a stationary wave displacement is the vector sum of the two opposite progressive wave displacements at each $x$ at the same instant.
Read the two $\text{mm}$ values at J near $6\text{ cm}$, at K near $11\text{ cm}$ and at L near $20.5\text{ cm}$, then use unknown equals stationary minus known.
walkthrough: Identify the curves: thin large-amplitude curve is the known progressive wave with amplitude $10\text{ mm}$, thick small-amplitude curve is the resultant stationary wave with amplitude $5\text{ mm}$.
State the physics: by the principle of superposition, $y_{stationary} = y_{known} + y_{other}$ at every position $x$ at the same time, so $y_{other} = y_{stationary} - y_{known}$.
At J, $x \approx 6\text{ cm}$: $y_{stationary} \approx -5\text{ mm}$ and $y_{known} \approx 0\text{ mm}$, so $y_{other} \approx -5 - 0 = -5\text{ mm}$.
At K, $x \approx 11\text{ cm}$: $y_{stationary} \approx +5\text{ mm}$ and $y_{known} \approx +5\text{ mm}$, so $y_{other} \approx +5 - 5 = 0\text{ mm}$.
At L, $x \approx 20.5\text{ cm}$: $y_{stationary} \approx 0\text{ mm}$ and $y_{known} \approx +10\text{ mm}$ near its crest, so $y_{other} \approx 0 - 10 = -10\text{ mm}$.
The set $-5$, $0$, $-10$ in $\text{mm}$ for J, K, L matches the table row. This is option A.

A.explanation: At J, K and L the sum of the two $\text{mm}$ readings equals the stationary wave displacement, giving $-5$, $0$ and $-10$.

B.explanation: These values do not add with the shown progressive wave to give the stationary wave values of about $-5$, $+5$ and $0$ at J, K and L.

C.explanation: This confuses the shown progressive wave value with the unknown one, for example it gives $0$ at J where the shown wave is already about $0$.

D.explanation: The signs are reversed by subtracting in the wrong order, so the sums do not reproduce the stationary wave displacement.
